mechanism: neutron-lib 2.14 moves packet_rate_limit into its QoS rule list, so Neutron appends the same type twice and changes the serialized QosRuleType object hash
repair_template: append the transitional target-owned QoS rule type only when the dependency does not already provide it

semantic_review.a1_failure: On the unchanged Neutron opening-cutoff snapshot, the pre-existing object-hash test passes with neutron-lib 2.13.0. With 2.14.0, the duplicated packet_rate_limit rule changes QosRuleType's computed hash from the checked reference and the single test fails; the exact maintainer patch restores it.
semantic_review.reviewer_basis: Reviewed the one-pin source opening diff, exact one-file production target diff, cutoff tox command, installed-version probes proving neutron-lib 2.13.0/2.14.0/2.14.0, patch applicability, and complete three-arm logs. The same pre-existing object-hash test runs in every arm; only A1 has the QosRuleType hash mismatch. The Python 3.8/tox 3/virtualenv 20 runner and source-era build constraints are identical across arms and only restore opening-era installation.
semantic_review.source_effect: The source opening changes exactly one upper-constraints pin, neutron-lib 2.13.0 to 2.14.0; version 2.14 adds packet_rate_limit to the dependency-owned VALID_RULE_TYPES list that the unchanged target also appends.
semantic_review.target_repair: The exact maintainer patch applies to the public opening-cutoff Neutron snapshot and conditionally appends the transitional target-owned rule only when neutron-lib does not already expose it. This preserves stable ordering and uniqueness under both dependency versions, changes production constants only, and deletes or skips no test.
